From: Asha Rao <dpo@novahealth.com>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Regional pinning acknowledgement + follow-up questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of NovaHealth's procurement sign-off we need a short written acknowledgement of a few operational commitments so our legal team can finalize the DPA addendum. Please confirm the following points in writing: 

1) Region pinning: when we provision the account with EU pinning, will all inference requests and telemetry be anchored to EU-only infrastructure by default?
2) Temporary cross-region processing: please describe the maximum duration and typical triggers that would allow transient processing outside the EU (e.g., burst capacity, disaster recovery). We need a clear upper bound and examples.
3) KMS / key material: does Redwood offer customer-managed keys for EU-pinned accounts and will keys ever be used outside the EU?
4) Subprocessors: please provide the current subprocessor roster for EU services and a target timeline for any new activations in the next 90 days.

I've attached our DPA questionnaire (answers in-line will be fine) and would appreciate a short acknowledgement and a draft timeline for the DPA addendum by end of next week.

Asha Rao
Data Protection Officer
NovaHealth

Attachment: novahealth_dpa_questions_20270510.pdf

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Asha Rao <dpo@novahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Regional pinning acknowledgement + follow-up questions

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. Below are short, operationally accurate answers we can provide now; we can follow with a DPA addendum draft the legal teams can sign.

1) Region pinning: EU-pinned accounts are served from EU-only inference clusters and telemetry collectors by default. Administrative control-plane metadata (account provisioning events) may touch our control plane which is logically separated and only stores minimal identifiers; no model request payloads or embeddings are transferred outside the designated EU serving region except under the limited conditions below.

2) Temporary cross-region processing: we allow transient cross-region processing in two narrow scenarios: (a) burst overflow when EU capacity is saturated and the customer has opted into burst failover (configurable per-account), and (b) disaster recovery when an EU region is unavailable. In both cases we provide advance notification where possible and we commit to the following operational bounds:
- Typical transient window: < 4 hours for autoscaling burst overflow in practice (most bursts complete in < 30 minutes).
- Maximum contractual window (for DR exercises or prolonged failover): 72 hours without an approved exception.
- All transient processing is logged, and payload-level egress is limited to the minimum required to complete the request (no long-lived cross-region replicas).

3) KMS / keys: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for EU-pinned deployments via our KMS integrations. When BYOK is enabled, key material never leaves the EU HSM boundary; keys are used only within EU-serving hosts.

4) Subprocessors: attached is our current EU-facing subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270501.csv). Short summary: primary compute: GCP (europe-west1) and Azure (northeurope) for reserved pools; object storage backups: AWS eu-central-1 (encrypted); telemetry pipeline: ElasticCloud hosted in eu-west-1. We do not use third-party model providers for core inference in EU-pinned accounts.

Next steps: we will prepare a short DPA addendum that encodes the 72-hour maximum failover window and the BYOK guarantees. Kimberly and Monica — can you confirm the roster and whether any subprocessor activations are scheduled in the next 90 days so we can include dates in the addendum?

Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270501.csv

Markus / Monica — confirming the internal checks completed: 

- Subprocessor roster is accurate as of 2027-05-01 (no new compute subprocessors planned in next 90 days). We have one telemetry vendor upgrade scheduled but it will remain EU-only.

We will add a clause in the addendum that transient processing is limited to 72 hours except by mutual written agreement.

Asha — happy to put this into the DPA addendum. Proposed next steps: 1) Legal teams exchange redlines via DocuSign link; 2) Redwood provides sample addendum PDF within 48 hours of receiving NovaHealth's preferred redlines; 3) Target signature within 2 weeks.
